structured_output.world_model:
E001 (9 epochs): acc 0.7430, time 9.43 s. E002 (10 epochs, since 9 epochs missed the bar): acc 0.7495, time 10.55 s. This is still 0.35 pp under 0.753, so it is not feasible.

Beliefs:
1. Epochs dominate time (H1). The two points give about 1.1 s per epoch, so a fixed cost of about 0 to 0.5 s is plausible. The measured accuracy slope is about 0.65 pp per epoch from 9 to 10. That is steeper than my earlier 0.4-0.6, which was a modest miss. It will probably flatten, so reaching 0.753 needs about 10.5-11 epochs, or other gains of about 0.4 pp. Time at that point is about 11.5-12 s.
2. Systems gains (H2.2). The eager port is probably partly launch-bound, but at batch 1024 with widths 128/384/576 on an A100, fp16 convs likely dominate. torch.compile max-autotune probably saves 3-10%. Risks: the autotune/compile cost lands in build (untimed, but the 600 s limit applies), and any recompile inside timed code. Foreach SGD saves little. The accuracy effect is about 0.
3. Noise. The per-seed accuracy std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.2 pp. The seeds are fixed, so repeat runs are partly correlated. GPU nondeterminism (cudnn.benchmark, atomics) still gives a run-to-run mean drift of about 0.1 pp. Time noise is about 1-3%. Any change under 0.2 pp is indistinguishable from noise.
4. EMA/Lookahead at 9-10 epochs is likely neutral or slightly helpful (about +0.1 pp), within noise.
5. Muon and progressive resizing are risky. Muon needs tuning and takes fewer steps at batch 2000, so I expect an accuracy loss. Progressive resizing at low resolution probably loses 0.5-1.5 pp for a time saving of about 15-25%, so it is not feasible on its own.
6. Regression. Gains from lucky seeds regress, so I shade claims downward.

Unsure: the true compile speedup, the fixed-cost share, and whether the 40-seed mean will sit below the 3-seed mean.

forecasts.reason: Compile likely gives a modest 3-10% gain; accuracy is unchanged within noise. It will not reach 0.753 by itself.
The EMA gain at about 10 epochs is likely 0-0.3 pp, within noise, and it adds a little time.
The rerun will land within about 0.2 pp and 3% of E002. That fits the per-seed std of 0.15-0.4 pp and the 2% time drift.

Dropping the ragged batch removes only a small shape cost; the saving is under 0.3 s and hard to separate from noise. n=50000 with bs=1024 already gives 48 full steps, and the train loop already uses only full batches.
Untuned Muon with half the steps will most likely lose accuracy and not cut epochs by 10%.
The saving is real but accuracy likely drops more than 0.2 pp; interpolation overhead and BN mismatch eat part of the gain.

cruxes: What is the run-to-run accuracy noise of the 3-seed mean (I005)? It decides whether 10 epochs at 0.7495 is truly short of the bar.
How launch-bound is the eager step? That is, how much does compile with foreach SGD save in timed seconds?
Does EMA or any other regularizer add at least 0.4 pp at about 10 epochs? That would close the gap without adding epochs.
